name: slop-check
description: Check any draft, document, pull request, chart or spec for the habits that mean nobody edited or reviewed it before it shipped, and name the specific lines. Also rewrites an answer that did not land into a shape the reader can act on. The em dash and choppy-run block runs here too, not only in Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Catch what nobody edited, and rewrite what did not land, in either host
interface.longDescription: The question worth asking about a piece of work is not whether a machine touched it, it is whether a person with judgement went through it afterwards. This checks for the habits that say nobody did: filler and machine vocabulary in prose, placeholders and swallowed errors in code, numbers too round to be measured in a chart, and options laid out with no recommendation in a spec. It names the specific lines, so a finding is something to act on or to send back. It also installs a hook that blocks em dashes and choppy sentence runs in the assistant's own writing, in Codex as well as in Claude Code, and the same check runs on request too. It also carries a second skill, say-it-simply, which rewrites an answer that confused the reader. That one comes from reading every message across ten days where the answer drew "I don't understand", and the finding that the failure is order rather than length. It reorders an answer around what the reader has to do, and replaces jargon rather than defining it.
defaultPrompt: Slop-check this before I post it.
Did anyone actually review this doc?
How much of this pull request looks unreviewed?
Check this spec for options with no recommendation.
Say that again in plain English.
